sentences.japanese: キング・ハンマーは少年を見下ろし、大きな笑い声をあげた。
sentences.reading: キング・ハンマーは しょうねんを みおろし、おおきな わらいごえを あげた。
sentences.romaji: Kingu Hanma wa shonen o mioroshi, ookina waraigoe o ageta.
sentences.english: King Hammer looked down at the boy and let out a booming laugh.
sentences.note: 見下ろす means to look down from above, physically or socially.

sentences.japanese: 姉を取り戻したければ、生き残れ！
sentences.reading: あねを とりもどしたければ、いきのこれ！
sentences.english: If you want your sister back, survive!
sentences.note: たければ means 'if you want to.' 生き残れ is the command form of 生き残る.

sentences.japanese: 戦うしかない。姉を救うために、もっと強くなる。
sentences.reading: たたかうしかない。あねを すくうために、もっと つよくなる。
sentences.romaji: Tatakau shika nai. Ane o sukuu tame ni, motto tsuyoku naru.
sentences.english: I have no choice. To save my sister, I must become stronger.
sentences.note: しかない means 'there is nothing but...' or 'there is no choice but to...'

sentences.reading: さあ、とうぎじょうへ はいれ！
sentences.note: 入れ is a direct command form of 入る, 'enter.'

sentences.japanese: 姉を返せ！オレは、あきらめない！
sentences.reading: あねを かえせ！オレは、あきらめない！
sentences.romaji: Ane o kaese! Ore wa, akiramenai!
sentences.english: Give my sister back! I will never give up!
sentences.note: あきらめない is the negative form of あきらめる, 'to give up.'

vocabulary.note: Common narration word for a young boy.
Can imply superiority when used in a confrontation.
声 attaches to show the sound of something.
Used for reclaiming something lost or stolen.
A useful resolve phrase in stories.

metadata.storyOrder: King Hammer forces Rio toward the arena trial.
